region.text: Dinguiraye, founded 1851 in the Kingdom of Tamba

ledger.note: 1852: Umar Tall defeats King Yambi of Tamba and founds his jihad state around Dinguiraye. "Founded Dinguiraye in the Kingdom of Tamba" in 1851; "September 1852: Defeated Yambi, who had attacked first. This began the conquest of Tamba." The Umar Tall page adds that he then "proclaimed a jihad", undated.

ledger.note: 1854: Umar Tall conquers Bambuk. "He conquered Bambuk in a rapid campaign (May-November 1854), and the Khasso kings submitted peacefully."

region.text: Diarra (Diara), the Soninke kingdom of north-western Mali east of Kaarta (the page gives no location; the disc is the one used in the kaarta dossier)

ledger.note: 31 May 1860: Umar Tall conquers Diarra. The last Diarra king, Biranté Karounga Diawara, was "captured and executed by Omar Saidou Tall on May 31, 1860" (Diarra page; infobox: conquered 1860). The page gives no outline: the region is the Diarra disc of the kaarta dossier, a stand-in.

1861: the capital moves from Nioro to Ségou.

region.text: Massina: Djenné, Hamdullahi, the Bandiagara area

ledger.note: 1862: Umar Tall attacks the Fulbe Massina state. The Toucouleur page lists "February 1861: Battles near Tio against the Massina-led coalition" and Cayawal (undated) before the fall of Djenné.

region.text: Massina: Djenné, Hamdullahi, the Bandiagara area

ledger.note: May 1862: Djenné falls, then Hamdullahi, the Massina capital.

region.text: Massina: Djenné, Hamdullahi, the Bandiagara area

ledger.note: 1862: Umar Tall conquers Massina. "May 1862: Djenné fell, followed by Hamdullahi"; Amadu III was captured and put to death at Cayawal. The Umar Tall page has conflicting dates for Hamdullahi (May 1862, reoccupied spring 1863).

region.text: Hamdullahi, the Massina capital just south of Mopti

ledger.note: February 1864: Massina rebels retake Hamdullahi and Umar Tall is killed (14 February, Degembere); his son Ahmadu succeeds. "Ba Lobbo's forces captured it in February 1864"; the Toucouleur page: "fled, but was killed soon after".

1884: Ahmadu moves his court to Nioro after Muntaga's revolt. "Muntaga ... rebelled in 1884, prompting Ahmadu to move his court to Nioro"; the Ahmadu Tall page has the revolt and the siege of Nioro in 1885.

region.text: Ségou and the Bambara heartland on the Niger

ledger.note: 1890: the French take Ségou. "Ségou fell to the French" about a year after Koundian (February 1889); no month on the page.

region.text: Kaarta, whose capital Nioro was seized in April 1855 (with Diafunu)

ledger.note: 1891: the French take Nioro and Kaarta. "They captured Nioro in 1891 and drove Ahmadu to Bandiagara." The Ahmadu Tall page has the French advance on Nioro in December 1890 (forces dispersed 23 December) and the city evacuated shortly afterward.

wars.outcome: French victories: Ségou 1890, Nioro 1891, Bandiagara 1893. The Treaty of Nango (February 1880) recognised the empire's borders but was never ratified; the Treaty of Gory (12 May 1887) made it a "nominal protectorate of France".
wars.note: 1878 September: French attack at Logo; 1882 December: Mourgala; Gory besieged 18 December 1886 to March 1888; Koundian seized by Archinard in February 1889.

certainty.note: Pages give no outline; the empire was a string of garrisons and provinces run by Umar's relatives. The Treaty of Nango (1880) recognised its borders but was never ratified.

notes:
Tukulor Empire, additions batch af-03-x (no Cliopatria row). Pages: Toucouleur Empire, Ahmadu Tall, Umar Tall (the three that gave dates), Louis Archinard and French Sudan (both thin). Page budget 5 used.

Conflicts: (1) Ségou fell 10 March 1861 (Toucouleur Empire page; the Bamana and Massina dossiers use the same) versus 10 March 1860 (Umar Tall page): 1861 followed. (2) Hamdullahi: May 1862 (Toucouleur page), reoccupied spring 1863 and lost February 1864 (both pages, with the Umar Tall page contradicting itself). (3) Muntaga's revolt 1884 (Toucouleur page) versus 1885 (Ahmadu Tall page). (4) Nioro: 1891 (Toucouleur page) versus an advance in December 1890 and evacuation "shortly afterward" (Ahmadu Tall page). (5) The Toucouleur infobox says 1852-1903; the text ends the empire in 1893 and the dissolve follows the text. (6) Nioro/Kaarta: April 1855 (Toucouleur Empire and Umar Tall pages) versus 1854 (the Kaarta page, opened for the kaarta dossier); 1855 followed, the kaarta dossier ends in April 1855.

Not on any page opened: an area; the outline between 1864 and 1890; Khasso (submitted 1854, rebelled later, not drawn); Makhana and Guidimakha; Timbuktu (Umar Tall was repulsed 1863); Futa Toro (only a sphere of influence under the 1860 treaty); the fate of Dinguiraye and Bambuk before 1893 (carried to the end at confidence 1 in the 1891 and 1893 keyframes); the dates of Archinard's Koundian-Ségou-Nioro-Bandiagara campaigns beyond what the Ahmadu Tall page gives.

For the french-africa dossier (af-08): the Treaty of Gory (12 May 1887) made the empire a nominal French protectorate (vassal tint 1887-1890); Ségou 1890, Nioro 1891, Bandiagara 1893 are French gains. For the Tidiani/Aguibou line at Bandiagara the pages say only that Tidiani Tall contested the succession and the French installed Aguibou in 1893.

Gazetteer: Bambuk (region, Kéniéba/Kédougou gold country) and Kaarta (region around Nioro du Sahel) and Bandiagara and Hamdullahi (places) are not in the gazetteer; proxies used (Kédougou admin1, Nioro du Sahel 150 km, Mopti 60 km). Wikidata id unknown (null).
